schemaNote: Round 4: the forward merge that resolves #2377's conflict. No product change of this issue's own.
summary: sjawhar/legion#2377 merged to main at dfd128f1 and overlaps this change, so GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING, which also costs it every check. This round is the forward merge of main at 9ab28e09 (head 806dbdaf) with the three resolutions #2377's reviewer recorded and nothing else, plus the census row the architect asked for, which now names the folded CHANGELOG.md lines and says this pull request does not correct them.

proof.criterion: The conflict with #2377 is resolved as recorded, and the merged code is the behaviour both changes describe: a failed rewatch reports nothing of its own while the resume path of #2377 stays.
proof.surface: The repository's Go test harness for every package either change touches, with the resolved files compiled and exercised: internal/kvwatch (the resume and the repair report), internal/bus, cmd/listener (whose restart test asserts main's resumed warm-up after every restart), cmd/dispatch and the separate packages/envoy/infra module.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go build ./... && go vet ./internal/bus/ ./internal/kvwatch/ ./cmd/listener/ && go test ./internal/kvwatch/ ./internal/bus/ -count=1 -timeout 30m && go test ./cmd/listener/ -count=1 -timeout 40m -skip '<the four Docker-only TestDispatch tests>' && go test ./cmd/dispatch/ -run 'Settings|Boot|Replica|Stream' -count=1; cd infra && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./aws/... ./render/... -count=1
proof.observed: build and vet exit 0; ok internal/kvwatch 63.491s, ok internal/bus 306.064s, ok cmd/listener 485.614s (which includes TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts asserting outcome 'resumed' with no entries after each restart, so #2377's side is exercised), ok cmd/dispatch 35.182s, ok infra/aws 7.109s, ok infra/aws/rendering 0.017s, ok infra/render 0.264s.
proof.negativeControl: The merge's own conflict markers are the control: with them in place the tree does not compile (go build fails on kvwatch.go), and the build above passes only because each of the three conflicts was resolved. A wrong resolution of the call shape (w.watch(kv, 0), main's old arity) fails the same build.

proof.criterion: Review round 1 item 1 and the architect's decision, re-driven at the merge head: a KV watch rebuild stalled past bus.RepairGrace answers /healthz 200 degraded naming the rebuild, the answer under the grace is unchanged, and the caches follow their buckets again once the fault is lifted.
proof.surface: The built envoy-listener binary against a real nats-server v2.10.29 with JetStream, restarted under a configuration denying only $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.KV_envoy_{interests,roles,sessions}.>; /healthz and GET /v1/interests/ over HTTP.
proof.observed: 200 healthy at start; 200 healthy after a plain NATS restart with the interest written then served and 0 ERROR lines; with the deny in place 200 healthy inside the grace, then 200 {"error":"KV watch rebuild unavailable: rewatch interest cache: watch interest registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded\nrewatch session cache: watch session registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded (no rebuild has succeeded for 1m0s)","status":"degraded"}; 200 healthy again once the deny was lifted, with a new interest served.
proof.negativeControl: At this branch's base 88840d35, as Go probes in a throwaway copy of the tree: TestBaseHealthzAnswersAHookStallPastAMinute fails ('/healthz 75 s into a rebuild that never succeeded = 200 map[... status:healthy]') and TestBaseRewatchRetryAfterAReconnectLogsNoError fails on the ERROR the base logs for a rewatch the retry repairs.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 3 at the head that merges: TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts passes 200 of 200 isolated runs, now against #2377's rewritten test body.
proof.surface: The listener's own harness, which builds and runs the listener against a real NATS, driven from packages/envoy/cmd/listener.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/cmd/listener && go test -c -o "$TMPDIR/listener-r4.test" . && for i in $(seq 1 200); do "$TMPDIR/listener-r4.test" -test.run '^TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts$' -test.count=1 >"$TMPDIR/r4-runs/run-$i.log" 2>&1; done (serial, one process per run, no -race)
proof.observed: 200 PASS, 0 FAIL at 806dbdaf, against the version of the test #2377 wrote, which asserts the resumed warm-up after each restart. The same loop ran 200/0 at 40e9841d, ee461d32, b7cccdc9 and a3b2b533.
proof.negativeControl: The same loop with 49 runs at the base 88840d35: 48 PASS, 1 FAIL, the failure being this issue's symptom (ERROR envoy nats reconnect hook failed ... rewatch session cache: open session registry KV bucket: context deadline exceeded).

proof.criterion: The pull request carries CI again: a conflicting head gets none, so the merge is what lets the lanes run for this code.
proof.surface: GitHub's own mergeability and Actions on the branch, read through the REST API.
proof.command: gh pr view 2504 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus; gh api 'repos/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs?branch=legion%2FINFRA-743'
proof.observed: Before this merge: CONFLICTING/DIRTY at 76c80ac5. The merge 806dbdaf was pushed as a code push whose head carries no skip-checks trailer, and the handoff follows in a push of its own. The lanes at the previous merge head 40e9841d had already run green or skipped with envoy-go-race, dispatch and dispatch-memory still going at the tester's read, which is the evidence that a non-conflicting head runs them.
proof.negativeControl: Round 3's record: three pushes while the pull request was conflicting (ee461d32, the empty 9c2ea00f and the handoff 5c47bed0, the last two carrying no trailer) produced 0 check runs each, and only the merge that cleared the conflict produced any.

filesChanged: No file of this issue's own change was edited this round. The merge 806dbdaf resolves three conflicts: internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go (Rewatch's doc keeps this change's failure sentence and #2377's resume paragraph; its body calls w.watch(kv, conn, 0) with no reportFailedRepair), packages/envoy/AGENTS.md (the reconnect bullet keeps this change's hook-failure sentence, the warm-up bullet keeps #2377's resumed text with this change's reason and both repairers named, and #2377's new session-cache bullet is kept whole), and the two pr-2362 changelog fragments, which main deleted when the fold moved them into packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md.

The pull request body's census now has its own row for those fragments and a row naming the folded CHANGELOG.md lines 64 and 93 under ## [22.1.0] - 2026-10-29, stating that this pull request does not correct them and why, with the runtime correction in cmd/dispatch/settings.go:83,85 named in their place.
trickyParts: A conflicting pull request gets no CI at all, so a conflict with a sibling that merged first costs the round its checks as well as its mergeability; the forward merge is the repair for both.

#2377's resume work and this change's deletion meet inside one function: Rewatch now takes conn for the resume and reports nothing of its own on failure. The listener's restart test, which #2377 rewrote to assert the resumed warm-up, is what exercises both sides together, and it is the test the 200-run loop drives.
discoveredComplexity: #2446 (INFRA-594) is still open and conflicts with main on its own in 18 files; against this head it adds cmd/listener/main.go, where this change's 200 degraded branch and its 503 'role lane subscription inactive' branch both belong. Its implementer has that resolution in writing.
This pod has two CPUs, so the tester and the implementer cannot both drive a smoke or a 200-run loop without spoiling each other's counts.
